        "All 61 owned diff lines in one JavaScript file were read. Four current-window screen availability values are copied once after prefill completion, the no-message guard and content-height sizing. snapToCorner uses that closure snapshot with current outer dimensions, rather than reading screen availability on each call. The initial move, resize listener and fallback use the same snap function. This is a cached coordinate source, not an explicit primary-monitor query in the original patch.",
        "The fixed accepted source is a later phase: it queries nsIScreenManager.primaryScreen.GetAvailRect in device coordinates, falls back to the window screen multiplied by devicePixelRatio, then divides the cached coordinates by the current ratio. It also sizes content before the initial snap. Those primary-screen/DPI refinements are not credited to this initial cache patch. No modified test or assertion exists.",
        "The full primary preserves the reporter's inability to obtain alerts under mozregression, the author's proposed screen-reassignment explanation, and later success reported for one linked Daily build with clean and copied profiles. The sparse review says Let's give it a try and has no actual inlines/history. These are attributed historical reports, not our OS geometry/race verification. The described native Thunderbird alert is the custom window; it is not proof of the OS notification route.",
        "Both required complete retained discussions are now read. The original current-window cache and accepted later primary-screen/device-coordinate implementation remain distinct; reporter success and author explanation stay attributed."
